title: Reuse the frozen generic scalable Boolean entailment method for satisfiability decisions
independentExamples: A satisfiable renamed CNF with two clauses and a validated assignment
An unsatisfiable pair of opposed unit clauses with a replayable DPLL certificate
A three-clause conflict preserved after variable permutation and clause reordering
preconditions: Every clause is non-empty and contains validated signed semantic variables.
The task creates a tautological Boolean query over the same formula language.
The scalable entailment method retains its default report-only inconsistency policy.
invariants: A consistent complete premise context maps to SAT only after its context model satisfies every source clause.
An inconsistent complete premise context maps to UNSAT only after independent certificate replay.
The adapter never selects an answer from source identity, record order, expected label, or puzzle vocabulary.
Resource limits retain the case and produce an explicit failed execution rather than a guessed label.
uncertaintySemantics: RESOURCE_LIMIT and malformed task states remain explicit and never map to SAT or UNSAT.
proofBehavior: SAT requires the generic solver's complete context model and a second direct clause check. UNSAT requires the generic full-context DPLL inconsistency certificate and independent verifier replay.

resourceBounds.inherited: The frozen scalable Boolean entailment defaults bound semantic atoms, CNF variables, clauses, and DPLL search nodes.
resourceBounds.denominator: A bound may affect execution status but cannot reduce source retention or an evaluation denominator.

kbMigration: None. No KB record, package, core method, capability descriptor, runtime route, or solver behavior changes.
decision: Reuse accepted generic core without modification. The only implementation is source validation, typed projection, oracle isolation, and scoring in the SATBench adapter.
